contentMap.targetAudience: Professionals and businesses creating high-quality visual content, including creative, marketing, design, and video production teams

hero.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
hero.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) - advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
hero.supportingLine: From text prompts, images, or scripts, generate professional visuals and videos with powerful multimodal AI systems.

productSections.name: Feature 1
productSections.headline: AI Image Generation with Seedream 4.5
productSections.description: Seedream 4.5 is a high-performance multimodal image generation system designed to produce high-resolution, high-fidelity images from text prompts and visual inputs. The model unifies text-to-image synthesis, image editing, and multi-image composition within a single framework.

features.title: Advanced Text–Image Alignment
features.description: Accurately translates prompts into visuals with improved semantic understanding.

features.title: High-Resolution Output
features.description: Generate native images up to 1K–4K resolution with strong visual fidelity.

features.title: Superior Typographic Rendering
features.description: Optimized for posters, ads, and text-heavy visual designs.

features.title: Multi-Image Composition with Identity Preservation
features.description: Combines multiple inputs while accurately maintaining subject consistency.

features.title: Strong Structural Fidelity
features.description: Maintains composition, layout, and scene structure with high precision.

productSections.headline: AI Video Generation with Seedance 1.5 Pro by Bytedance
productSections.description: Seedance 1.5 Pro is a next-generation generative model designed for native audio-visual generation, enabling synchronized creation of video and sound together. Built on a dual-branch diffusion transformer architecture, the model integrates cross-modal learning to produce coherent visual and audio outputs.

features.title: Text-to-Video Generation
features.description: Create videos directly from text prompts.

features.title: Audio-Visual Synchronization
features.description: Generate video and audio simultaneously with strong multimodal alignment.

features.title: Multilingual Lip-Sync
features.description: Supports multilingual and dialect-level lip synchronization.

features.title: Cinematic Camera Control
features.description: Generate videos with dynamic camera movement and cinematic storytelling.

features.title: 10× Faster Inference
features.description: Optimized inference pipeline significantly improves generation speed.

plans.name: Seedream 4.5 (AI Image Generation)

plans.name: Seedance 1.5 Pro (AI Video Generation)

referenceMap.heroPattern: Top-loaded split hero with brand/logo at upper left, oversized headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet list of benefit statements. Primary visual emphasis is typographic rather than media-led. Hero uses strong vertical stacking and a single dominant CTA nearby.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-page linear flow: hero/banner first, then a lead-capture form card, followed by content sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing and surface changes rather than complex navigation. Information is presented in progressively detailed blocks.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content cards with minimal decoration, strong borders or subtle shadow treatment, and dense text lists. Utility-first feel over ornamental styling. Form and content areas appear as distinct boxed modules.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a high-contrast action in the hero and repeated within content sections. CTA pattern favors one main conversion action per section, with form-led conversion as the primary path. Secondary CTA is either absent or de-emphasized.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module in the reference layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference HTML, so no reusable footer pattern can be reliably inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible layout; brand logo functions as the only explicit media element. Content relies on text hierarchy and lists rather than image grids, video embeds, or hero illustrations.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with a headline, supporting description, then a feature list of short title-plus-description items. Progressive disclosure is achieved through sequential sections rather than tabs or accordions. Feature blocks are optimized for scanability.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead form card placed directly after hero content, acting as the main conversion module. Form is dense and enterprise-oriented, with multiple hidden fields and a single visible submission flow. The form is framed as a separate boxed surface to distinguish conversion from marketing content.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation system is evident from the reference HTML; any movement is likely limited to basic page scripting or optional carousel behavior in commented code, not core to the design pattern.
designNotes: Typography and hierarchy do most of the visual work.
Content is organized for fast scanning and lead capture.
Avoids decorative complexity; relies on clear sections and compact modules.
Reusable pattern is best suited to B2B product pages with a single primary action.

personality.productType: AI image and video generation platform
personality.buyer: Creative, marketing, design, and video production teams at businesses needing high-quality generative visual content
personality.reasoning: This is a generative AI product for creating images and videos, so it must follow the cinematic-ai theme family. The brand color set is tightly constrained by Techjockey’s brand palette, so the page should use the brand’s orange as the primary identity rather than an unrelated purple-gradient system. Because the offer combines high-end image and video generation, the visual language should feel premium, intelligent, and media-forward, with layered product storytelling, dark contrast, and interactive split sections that separate Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro clearly.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so the hero needs a smaller but still bold size to preserve hierarchy and avoid wrapping overload.

colours.colourReason: Brand identity must come from Techjockey’s primary orange (#ff6b00). Since the product is AI, the dark cinematic base is appropriate, but the accent, CTA, and hero emphasis should remain brand-led rather than generic purple or blue.

layout.heroBackground: dark cinematic background with layered product mockups and floating media chips
layout.heroReason: The content describes two distinct AI engines, so a split layout lets the copy explain value on the left while the right side showcases visual generations, timelines, and media outputs in a premium collage.
layout.featureReason: Seedream and Seedance should be separated into distinct sections with alternating contrast so each model gets its own visual identity and the page feels editorial rather than repetitive.
layout.darkSectionFor: Hero, model-introduction sections, and feature deep-dives; lighter sections for pricing/cart and trust blocks

personality.imageryDirection: Use high-fidelity AI media composites: abstract generated portraits, poster-style typography samples, cinematic video frames, timeline strips, and UI shells showing prompt-to-output workflows. Hero visual should feel like a premium creative studio dashboard with floating preview cards, audio waveforms, and generation controls.
personality.designPersonality: Premium cinematic AI studio with brand-orange authority, dark immersive contrast, layered glass panels, and polished product storytelling built for creative teams that want speed, control, and enterprise-grade visual quality.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a centered or strongly stacked hero with dark, authoritative background treatment and high-contrast white text. Prioritize typography over imagery, with the CTA placed immediately below the supporting copy. Keep the benefit list compact and scannable.
layoutStrategy.features: Present Seedream and Seedance as two consecutive technical capability sections using the same card system to create parity and easy comparison. Maintain generous vertical separation between sections and avoid complex navigation. Use clean white surfaces and structured grids.
layoutStrategy.proof: Use testimonials as the primary trust layer since no badges or customer counts are available. Keep proof visually lightweight but credible, with role labels and gold star treatment. Do not introduce awards or other unprovided trust modules.
layoutStrategy.pricing: Use a light grey pricing area with elevated cards. Make quote-led conversion the default pattern, while showing the starting price only where provided. Ensure both plans have a clear CTA and concise included-feature checklists.
layoutStrategy.form: Do not include a lead form because the input explicitly excludes it. Use CTAs routed to quote or demo request intent instead.

designIntent.tokenProfileHint: Default to Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and Inter for body, with a deep trust-authority palette adapted for AI/enterprise credibility. Use dark hero treatment, neutral whites and greys for content surfaces, and a strong accent for CTAs and pricing emphasis.
designIntent.figmaReadySummary: Design a high-density B2B category landing page that leads with a typographic hero, then separates the two products into parallel feature sections, followed by quote-led pricing and testimonial proof. The page should feel technical, trustworthy, and conversion-focused without using a form or media-heavy hero. Keep the system consistent: dark hero, white feature cards, light grey pricing band, and minimal footer.

figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: marketing: Sora heading + Inter body; use a strong brand-accent hero with dark-purple primary and warm accent CTA treatment suitable for generative AI / marketing audiences.

sections.variantHint: top-loaded banner with logo at upper left, oversized headline, short supporting paragraph, compact bullet benefits, primary CTA only
sections.notes: Use a strong solid hero background per brand rules. Since no media asset is provided, keep the hero typographic and vertical. Include the brand/logo position at upper-left and place the CTA directly under the supporting copy. Use the extras benefit line as a compact checklist block inside the hero. Secondary CTA is intentionally absent in content; do not invent one.

sections.variantHint: light surface strip with inline benefit statements and optional trust stats
sections.notes: Create a slim separator strip after the hero using the provided checkmarked benefit statements. No badges/customer count are provided in the source, so keep this as a simple value-prop bar rather than award-proof. Use divider spacing to maintain section rhythm.

sections.variantHint: centered boxed card, form-first conversion module
sections.notes: The input form block has no explicit fields/headline/CTA in contentMap, so build a compact lead-capture card shell with standard Techjockey form structure placeholders only if wired from the template system. If the system cannot infer fields from the content, keep this section as a reserved conversion card container without visible field labels. This section exists because the reference rhythm requires a lead-capture module after hero.

sections.variantHint: 3-column feature card grid with section intro above cards and CTA repeated in header
sections.notes: Represent Seedream 4.5 capabilities as a clean feature section. Use a section intro row with headline and description, followed by a 3-column grid of five cards. Keep cards uniform and text-dense. Include the section CTA near the intro or at the end of the block. Since all feature items have no icons, use the text-first card pattern from the system without invented graphics.

sections.variantHint: 3-column feature card grid with section intro above cards
sections.notes: Represent Seedance 1.5 Pro capabilities in a second feature section immediately after Seedream. Use the same card system for consistency, but vary the intro copy and feature titles to clearly differentiate video generation. No CTA is provided in this product section, so do not add one. Keep the section rhythm consistent and linear.

sections.frameName: Standard Features / Advanced Capabilities of Seedream 4.5
sections.variantHint: text-led capability callout with short description block and dense utility list treatment
sections.notes: Use the provided extras content to create a secondary informational block for Seedream advanced capabilities. This should be a text-led section with a concise headline and description, visually differentiated from the primary product feature grid through a more compact card or callout surface. Do not introduce new claims beyond the supplied extras text.

sections.frameName: Additional Feature / Key Capabilities of Seedance 1.5 Pro
sections.variantHint: text-led capability callout with narrative coherence and motion emphasis
sections.notes: Mirror the Seedream capability block but position it as a sibling section for Seedance. Keep it lightweight and consistent, using the provided headline and description as the only copy source. No extra media is required.

sections.variantHint: 2-card pricing grid with centered quote cards; one plan may show starting price, both use quote CTA
sections.notes: Although the reference pattern says pricing may be absent, the contentMap explicitly provides pricing plans, so include a pricing section. Use two cards side-by-side on desktop. The Seedance plan should surface the starting price; the Seedream plan appears as quote-only with no price. Keep the CTA per plan as provided. Use the includes checklist formatting mandated by design memory. Do not invent EMI because it is not supplied.

sections.variantHint: 3-column testimonial cards with gold star row, italic quotes, bold author line
sections.notes: Render five testimonials in a 3-column grid with card wrapping. Follow the testimonial card system: left accent border, star row, italicized quote, author name, designation, and company line. Since company is empty in all cases, omit company text rather than filling placeholder values.

sections.variantHint: compact footer with required legal/navigation placeholders and cart label if supported
sections.notes: The extras include Footer and CART, but no detailed footer content is supplied. Build a minimal closing footer frame using standard Techjockey footer shell only. Keep it understated and avoid adding unsupported navigation taxonomy. If CART is referenced by template logic, expose it only as a small utility label or footer meta item, not as a shopping cart flow.

sections.variantHint: single-column hero with CTA under copy and benefit bullets below
sections.notes: Stack everything vertically for mobile. Keep the hero text-led and compact, with the primary CTA full-width. Preserve the benefit checklist but reduce it to concise lines. No media is available, so do not add an image placeholder.

sections.variantHint: compact stacked value-prop list
sections.notes: Convert the trust/benefit strip into a compact stacked module on mobile to preserve readability. Keep it lightweight and avoid multi-column compression.

sections.variantHint: full-width form card with single-column field stack
sections.notes: Use the same lead capture shell as desktop, but stack all elements vertically and make the card full-width. If form fields are not explicitly available, keep the card reserved for template-driven form injection rather than inventing inputs.

sections.variantHint: single-column feature cards with section intro above list
sections.notes: On mobile, convert the five feature cards into a single-column stack. Keep each card tight and readable. The section CTA, if shown, should be full-width and placed after the intro copy or at the end of the feature list.

sections.variantHint: single-column feature cards with section intro above list
sections.notes: Keep the Seedance section consistent with Seedream while maintaining clear separation between products. Use full-width cards and allow natural vertical scrolling. No CTA should be added because none exists in source content.

sections.variantHint: compact text-led callout
sections.notes: Keep the advanced capabilities section compact and text-first. Stack the headline and description with generous spacing between adjacent sections.

sections.variantHint: compact text-led callout
sections.notes: Mirror the Seedream capability section in mobile format. Keep it light and easy to scan.

sections.variantHint: stacked quote cards with full-width CTA buttons
sections.notes: Stack the two pricing cards vertically. Ensure the Seedance starting price remains prominent. Keep all CTAs full-width and preserve the includes checklist within each card.

sections.variantHint: single-column testimonial cards, optionally horizontally scrollable if needed by template system
sections.notes: Stack testimonial cards in a single column for easy reading. Maintain the star row, italic quote, and author block. Do not attempt a carousel unless the design system already supports one; the safer default is vertical stacking.

sections.variantHint: condensed footer shell
sections.notes: Use a compact footer shell only. Avoid adding detailed navigation rows that are not supported by the supplied content.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use a single-page linear flow with consistent vertical spacing between sections and subtle background changes to separate content blocks.
Maintain the same component families across desktop and mobile; only change layout direction and density, not the underlying patterns.
Because the input provides no media assets or badges, keep the page text-led and do not fabricate logos, customer counts, or image placeholders.
Follow the contentMap strictly: include both product feature sections, both capability callouts from extras, pricing, testimonials, and the form shell.
Use Techjockey’s design-system defaults for cards, CTAs, and typography; this page should feel structured, conversion-oriented, and B2B credible.
